1.text: Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ by tha commandment of God our Saviour, N Lord Jesus Christ, which is our hope;
2 Timothy, my own son in tha faith: Grace, mercy, N peace, from God our Father N Jesus Christ our Lord.
As I besought u 2 abide still at Ephesus, when I went in2 Macedonia, dat u might charge some dat dey teach no other doctrine,
Neither give heed 2 fables N endless genealogies, which minister questions, rather than godly edifying which is in faith: so do.
Now tha end of tha commandment is charity out of a pure heart, N of a good conscience, N of faith unfeigned:
From which some havin swerved have turned aside 2 vain jangling;
Desiring 2 be teachers of tha law; understanding neither what dey say, nor whereof dey affirm.
But we know dat tha law is good, if a man use it lawfully;
Knowin dis, dat tha law is not made 4 a righteous man, but 4 tha lawless N disobedient, 4 tha ungodly N 4 sinners, 4 unholy N profane, 4 murderers of fathers N murderers of mothers, 4 manslayers,
4 whoremongers, 4 ’em dat defile themselves wit mankind, 4 menstealers, 4 liars, 4 perjured persons, N if there be any other thing dat is contrary 2 sound doctrine;
According 2 tha glorious gospel of tha blessed God, which was committed 2 my trust.
N I thank Christ Jesus our Lord, who has enabled me, 4 dat he counted me faithful, puttin me in2 tha ministry;
Who was before a blasphemer, N a persecutor, N injurious: but I obtained mercy, because I did it ignorantly in unbelief.
N tha grace of our Lord was exceeding abundant wit faith N love which is in Christ Jesus.
Dis is a faithful sayin, N worthy of all acceptation, dat Christ Jesus came in2 tha world 2 save sinners; of whom I am chief.
But 4 dis cause I obtained mercy, dat in me first Jesus Christ might show forth all longsuffering, 4 a pattern 2 ’em which should hereafter believe on him 2 life everlasting.
Now 2 tha King eternal, immortal, invisible, tha only wise God, be honour N glory 4 ever N ever. Amen.
Dis charge I commit 2 u, son Timothy, according 2 tha prophecies which went before on u, dat u by ’em might war a good warfare;
Holding faith, N a good conscience; which some havin put away concerning faith have made shipwreck:
Of whom is Hymenaeus N Alexander; whom I have delivered 2 Satan, dat dey may learn not 2 blaspheme.

2.text: I exhort therefore, dat, first of all, supplications, prayers, intercessions, N givin of thanks, be made 4 all men;
4 kings, N 4 all dat r in authority; dat we may lead a quiet N peaceable life in all godliness N honesty.
4 dis is good N acceptable in tha sight of God our Saviour;
Who will have all men 2 be saved, N 2 come 2 tha knowledge of tha truth.
4 there is one God, N one mediator between God N men, tha man Christ Jesus;
Who gave himself a ransom 4 all, 2 be testified in due time.
Whereunto I am ordained a preacher, N an apostle, (I speak tha truth in Christ, N lie not;) a teacher of tha Gentiles in faith N verity.
I will therefore dat men pray every where, liftin up holy hands, without wrath N doubting.
In like manner also, dat women adorn themselves in modest clothing, wit shamefacedness N sobriety; not wit broided hair, or gold, or pearls, or costly array;
But (which becomes women professing godliness) wit good works.
Let tha woman learn in silence wit all subjection.
But I suffer not a woman 2 teach, nor 2 usurp authority over tha man, but 2 be in silence.
4 Adam was first formed, then Eve.
N Adam was not deceived, but tha woman bein deceived was in tha transgression.
Even so she shall be saved in childbearing, if dey continue in faith N charity N holiness wit sobriety.

3.text: Dis is a true sayin, If a man desire tha office of a bishop, he desires a good work.
A bishop then must be blameless, tha husband of one wife, vigilant, sober, of good behaviour, given 2 hospitality, apt 2 teach;
Not given 2 wine, no striker, not greedy of filthy lucre; but patient, not a brawler, not covetous;
One dat rules well his own house, havin his children in subjection wit all gravity;
(4 if a man know not how 2 rule his own house, how shall he take care of tha church of God?)
Not a novice, lest bein lifted up wit pride he fall in2 tha condemnation of tha devil.
Moreover he must have a good report of ’em which r without; lest he fall in2 reproach N tha snare of tha devil.
Likewise must tha deacons be grave, not doubletongued, not given 2 much wine, not greedy of filthy lucre;
Holding tha mystery of tha faith in a pure conscience.
N let dese also first be proved; then let ’em use tha office of a deacon, bein found blameless.
Even so must their wives be grave, not slanderers, sober, faithful in all things.
Let tha deacons be tha husbands of one wife, ruling their children N their own houses well.
4 dey dat have used tha office of a deacon well purchase 2 themselves a good degree, N great boldness in tha faith which is in Christ Jesus.
Dese things write I 2 u, hoping 2 come 2 u shortly:
But if I tarry long, dat u may know how u ought 2 behave urself in tha house of God, which is tha church of tha livin God, tha pillar N ground of tha truth.

N without controversy great is tha mystery of godliness: God was manifest in tha flesh, justified in tha Spirit, seen of angels, preached 2 tha Gentiles, believed on in tha world, received up in2 glory.

4.text: Now tha Spirit speaks expressly, dat in tha latter times some shall depart from tha faith, givin heed 2 seducing spirits, N doctrines of devils;
Speakin lies in hypocrisy; havin their conscience seared wit a hot iron;
Forbidding 2 marry, N commanding 2 abstain from meats, which God has created 2 be received wit thanksgiving of ’em which believe N know tha truth.
4 every creature of God is good, N nothing 2 be refused, if it be received wit thanksgiving:
4 it is sanctified by tha word of God N prayer.
If u put tha brothers in remembrance of dese things, u will be a good minister of Jesus Christ, nourished up in tha words of faith N of good doctrine, whereunto u have attained.
But refuse profane N old wives’ fables, N exercise urself rather 2 godliness.
4 bodily exercise profits little: but godliness is profitable 2 all things, havin promise of tha life dat now is, N of dat which is 2 come.
Dis is a faithful sayin N worthy of all acceptation.
4 therefore we both labour N suffer reproach, because we trust in tha livin God, who is tha Saviour of all men, specially of dose dat believe.
Let no man despise ur youth; but be u an example of tha believers, in word, in conversation, in charity, in spirit, in faith, in purity.
Till I come, give attendance 2 reading, 2 exhortation, 2 doctrine.
Neglect not tha gift dat is in u, which was given u by prophecy, wit tha laying on of tha hands of tha presbytery.
Meditate upon dese things; give urself wholly 2 ’em; dat ur profiting may appear 2 all.
Pay attention 2 urself, N 2 tha doctrine; continue in ’em: 4 in doin dis u will both save urself, N ’em dat hear u.

5.text: Rebuke not an elder, but intreat him as a father; N tha younger men as brothers;
Tha elder women as mothers; tha younger as sisters, wit all purity.
Honour widows dat r widows indeed.
But if any widow have children or nephews, let ’em learn first 2 show piety at home, N 2 requite their parents: 4 dat is good N acceptable before God.
Now she dat is a widow indeed, N desolate, trusts in God, N continueth in supplications N prayers night N day.
But she dat lives in pleasure is dead while she lives.
N dese things give in charge, dat dey may be blameless.
But if any provide not 4 his own, N specially 4 dose of his own house, he has denied tha faith, N is worse than an infidel.
Don’t let a widow be taken in2 tha number under threescore years old, havin been tha wife of one man,

Well reported of 4 good works; if she have brought up children, if she have lodged strangers, if she have washed tha saints’ feet, if she have relieved tha afflicted, if she have diligently followed every good work.
But tha younger widows refuse: 4 when dey have begun 2 wax wanton against Christ, dey will marry;
Havin damnation, because dey have cast off their first faith.
N withal dey learn 2 be idle, wandering about from house 2 house; N not only idle, but tattlers also N busybodies, speakin things which dey ought not.
I will therefore dat tha younger women marry, bear children, guide tha house, give none occasion 2 tha adversary 2 speak reproachfully.
4 some r already turned aside after Satan.
If any man or woman dat believes have widows, let ’em relieve ’em, N don’t let tha church be charged; dat it may relieve ’em dat r widows indeed.
Let tha elders dat rule well be counted worthy of double honour, especially dey who labour in tha word N doctrine.
4 tha scripture says, u will not muzzle tha ox dat treads out tha corn. N, tha labourer is worthy of his reward.
Against an elder receive not an accusation, but before two or three witnesses.
’em dat sin rebuke before all, dat others also may fear.
I charge u before God, N tha Lord Jesus Christ, N tha elect angels, dat u observe dese things without preferring one before another, doin nothing by partiality.
Lay hands suddenly on no man, neither be partaker of other men’s sins: keep urself pure.
Drink no longer water, but use a little wine 4 ur stomach’s sake N thine often infirmities.
Some men’s sins r open beforehand, goin before 2 judgment; N some men dey follow after.
Likewise also tha good works of some r manifest beforehand; N dey dat r otherwise cannot be hid.

6.text: Let as many servants as r under tha yoke count their own masters worthy of all honour, dat tha name of God N his doctrine don’t be blasphemed.
N dey dat have believin masters, let ’em not despise ’em, because dey r brothers; but rather do ’em service, because dey r faithful N beloved, partakers of tha benefit. dese things teach N exhort.
If any man teach otherwise, N consent not 2 wholesome words, even tha words of our Lord Jesus Christ, N 2 tha doctrine which is according 2 godliness;
He is proud, knowin nothing, but doting about questions N strifes of words, whereof comes envy, strife, railings, evil surmisings,
Perverse disputings of men of corrupt minds, N destitute of tha truth, supposing dat gain is godliness: from such withdraw urself.
But godliness wit contentment is great gain.
4 we brought nothing in2 dis world, N it is certain we can carry nothing out.
N havin food N clothing let us be wit it content.
But dey dat will be rich fall in2 temptation N a snare, N in2 many foolish N hurtful lusts, which drown men in destruction N perdition.
4 tha love of money is tha root of all evil: which while some coveted after, dey have erred from tha faith, N pierced themselves through wit many sorrows.
But u, O man of God, flee dese things; N follow after righteousness, godliness, faith, love, patience, meekness.
Fight tha good fight of faith, lay hold on eternal life, whereunto u r also called, N have professed a good profession before many witnesses.
I give u charge in tha sight of God, who quickeneth all things, N before Christ Jesus, who before Pontius Pilate witnessed a good confession;
Dat u keep dis commandment without spot, unrebukeable, until tha appearing of our Lord Jesus Christ:
Which in his times he shall show, who is tha blessed N only Potentate, tha King of kings, N Lord of lords;
Who only has immortality, livin in tha light which no man can approach 2; whom no man has seen, nor can see: 2 whom be honour N power everlasting. Amen.
Charge ’em dat r rich in dis world, dat dey don’t be highminded, nor trust in uncertain riches, but in tha livin God, who gives us richly all things 2 enjoy;
Dat dey do good, dat dey be rich in good works, ready 2 distribute, willin 2 communicate;
Laying up in store 4 themselves a good foundation against tha time 2 come, dat dey may lay hold on eternal life.
O Timothy, keep dat which is committed 2 ur trust, avoiding profane N vain babblings, N oppositions of science falsely so called:
Which some professing have erred concerning tha faith. Grace be wit u. Amen.
